subject: gov.policy
name: Circular on the governance of public establishments and enterprises
milestone: Signed 28 August 2026
position_end: Directing ministers, secretaries of state, heads of public enterprises and state controllers to adopt strategic action plans on governance and performance, invoking among its bases the 2020 decree-law on electronic data exchange between public bodies

subject: gov.policy
name: Communication technologies ministry annual performance plan
milestone: 2025 edition names the national digital strategy as its operative framework
position_end: The ministry's 2025 performance plan names a National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 as the operative framework and anchors it in Vision 2035 and the 2023-2025 development plan
note: the plan dates the national strategy 2021-2025 where other sources in this ledger give 2020-2025, and nothing reconciles the two

subject: gov.policy
name: Customs administration strategic plan 2026-2030
milestone: Plan and governance charter presented at a working session, reported 2026-08-28
position_end: A 2026-2030 plan built around digitisation, presented with a governance charter, its axes covering border protection, an environment for attracting foreign investment, revenue collection, working methods and social responsibility, with assignment letters issued to central and regional customs structures for human resources, risk management and infrastructure
note: the plan document itself is not published

subject: gov.policy
name: Data-localisation rule for credit-information companies
milestone: Decree-law 2022-2 gazetted 4 January 2022
position_end: A sectoral decree-law bars credit-information companies from transferring their databases or hosting their data-protection sites outside Tunisia, and separately bars cloud hosting of credit information
note: the only express localisation rule on the record; the public-sector cloud labelling regime is a hosting-label scheme, not a general localisation statute

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital content of the development plan annex
milestone: All three volumes of the annex held, June 2026
position_start: Not held; the plan's digital content was known only from official statements about it (2025-08)
position_end: Held in full: the sectoral volume mentions digital or digitalisation 414 times, artificial intelligence 119, data 72 and cybersecurity 9, makes the digital economy a pillar of human-capital development, and commits to integration into the global digital landscape while preserving digital sovereignty (2026-06)

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Tunisia 2020-2025
milestone: Lapsed at term at the end of 2025
position_start: In force in its final year (2025-08)
position_end: Lapsed; no extension, repeal or outcomes report is held, so what it delivered against its own objectives is unestablished (2026-08)

subject: gov.policy
name: Ministerial council on digitalisation
milestone: Council held under the head of government 2026-08-18
position_end: A ministerial council devoted to digitalisation, chaired by the head of government, who stated that digitalisation is a necessity rather than a choice
note: the decisions taken at the council are not itemised in the record held

subject: gov.policy
name: National digital transformation vision
milestone: Ministerial council placed 192 projects under national follow-up and declared 2026 the launch year
position_start: Did not exist; the sectoral strategy that preceded it was in its final year (2025-08)
position_end: A chapter of the five-year development plan coordinated by the economy and planning ministry rather than a sectoral strategy owned by the communication technologies ministry, with 192 digital-transformation projects under cabinet follow-up (2026-02)
note: A change of instrument type, not a renewal: what the wiki and outside commentary called a national digital strategy is a plan chapter.

subject: gov.policy
name: National very-high-speed broadband strategy
milestone: Second fibre infrastructure-sharing consultation, 6 March to 2 April 2026
position_start: A ministry strategy for very-high-speed broadband development, with published terms of reference for a national fibre-to-the-home rollout dated 2013
position_end: The regulator opened a second public consultation on sharing fibre access infrastructure, running 6 March to 2 April 2026, after a first that ran from 26 September to 26 November 2025
note: the strategy page carries no publication date and its year is inferred from its own annexed specifications; no later broadband strategy, coverage target or take-up series is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Compulsory e-invoicing (Article 53)
milestone: Amendment bill 2026/012 debated in joint committee, February 2026
position_start: Article 53 of the 2026 finance law extended mandatory electronic invoicing to service-provision operations from 1 January 2026, and a tax administration note applied it to providers already enrolled in the national e-invoicing network, keeping paper transitionally for those who had not completed enrolment (2026-01)
position_end: Under amendment: parliament's memo records that no unified national e-invoicing system yet exists and that mass e-invoicing raises serious personal- and professional-data protection issues, and the amendment mandates a 30-day joint ministerial report on readiness and data-protection compliance before a phased timeline (2026-02)
note: the primary enactment and its operating note are now held; the February amendment builds on them rather than contradicting them

subject: gov.legislate
name: Decree-law 2020-31 on interoperability and electronic exchange
milestone: Approved by law 2021-14 of 7 April 2021, with modalities set by decree 2020-777
position_start: Defines interoperability and the interoperability platform, designates the national computing centre as sole operator, requires interoperability to identify persons through the citizen unique identifier and enterprise unique identifier registers, and bars bodies from re-asking users for data reachable through the platform
position_end: Unchanged in law and still the operative basis for the national platform; the implementing decree creates the operator's duties, a strategic committee tasked with piloting the national interoperability strategy, and a coordination committee
note: neither committee publishes minutes, membership or a strategy document

subject: gov.legislate
name: Decree-Law 2023-17 on cybersecurity
milestone: Gazetted 11 March 2023, the agency rename taking effect six months later
position_end: The decree-law creates the national cybersecurity agency, which succeeds and replaces the information security agency created in 2004, and establishes the G-Cloud and N-Cloud provider labelling regime for hosting; the rename took effect six months after publication
note: no implementing text, label register or list of labelled providers is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Development Plan 2026-2030 (loi n 2026-16)
milestone: Promulgated 20 July 2026 after adoption by both chambers
position_start: Did not exist as an adopted instrument
position_end: Promulgated as the binding reference for public policy to 2030 under articles 75 and 77 of the Constitution, adopted by the Assembly on 10 July and the Council of Regions on 17 July (2026-07)
note: Every volume of the annex held is marked draft; whether the promulgated annex differs from the version tabled and voted is not established, and no as-enacted printing has been published.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Law 2000-83 on electronic exchanges and commerce
milestone: In force since 2000, no repeal or replacement located
position_start: Gives electronic documents and signatures the evidential standing of writing, creates the national electronic certification agency, licenses certification service providers, and sets pre-contractual disclosure duties, a ten-working-day withdrawal right and electronic-payment-instrument liability rules for online sales
position_end: Unchanged; a bill on marketing and promotion through websites and social networks was still in committee as at September 2026

subject: gov.legislate
name: Law 2016-48 on banks and financial institutions
milestone: The operative statute for the payment-institution licensing regime
position_start: Brings electronic money within means of payment, covers remote and electronic payment services, and creates the payment-institution licensing regime, payment accounts, segregation of client funds and the central bank's rule-making power
position_end: Unchanged; the central bank's mobile-payment and domestic-payment circulars are made under it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Law 99-32 on the national statistical system
milestone: In force since 1999 and still listed by the statistics institute as governing law
position_start: Sets the principles of statistical activity, scientific independence, statistical secrecy including a sixty-year non-disclosure rule, and the duty to respond, and constitutes the national statistical council and the statistics institute
position_end: Unchanged in law; a replacement covering big data and administrative-data access is in drafting and no amending or replacing statute has been located

subject: gov.legislate
name: Legal and regulatory framework for artificial intelligence
milestone: Drafting begun, on the minister's statement of 25 May 2026
position_end: The communication technologies ministry has begun drafting legal and regulatory frameworks for responsible artificial-intelligence use, covering data protection, privacy and digital sovereignty, as the governance pillar of the still-unpublished national strategy; no artificial-intelligence law, decree or gazetted instrument exists
note: a statement of intent at a professional conference; no draft text, timetable or consultation is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Organic Law 2016-22 on access to information
milestone: Oversight authority without a president since its council's mandate lapsed in 2024
position_start: In force: the statute creates the national access-to-information authority, a proactive-publication duty, request and appeal procedures and sanctions, and repeals the two 2011 decree-laws it replaced
position_end: The statute is unamended, but the government confirmed in December 2025 that the authority has run without a president or vice-president since its nine-member council's mandate lapsed, which blocks legally valid meetings and has suspended staff allowances; the authority itself calls for urgent legislative revision
note: institutional paralysis rather than amendment: no text has changed the 2016 regime

subject: gov.legislate
name: Organic Laws 22 and 23 of 2024 on biometric identity
milestone: Adopted by parliament, 6 March 2024
position_start: In force: the card is issued by the interior ministry's specialised services, carries a secure electronic chip and an electronic authentication certificate and is mandatory from age 15; use was targeted for the first half of 2025 and unconfirmed (2025-08)
position_end: In force; nothing held confirms issuance has begun, and an amendment to prohibit a centralised biometric database held by the interior ministry was introduced the day before the vote and dismissed (2026-08)
sources: 2024-03-11-loi-organique-2024-22-carte-identite-nationale|2024-03-07 Eight years in the making - Tunisia's Biometric ID and Passport Bills risk rights|2024-04-23 Tunisia - Biometric ID card and passport usage to begin in H1 2025|2024-04-23 Tunisia to Get Biometric IDs in H1 of 2025
note: the primary text is now held: organic law 2024-22 amends the 1993 identity-card law. Civil society records that committee deliberations lacked public consultation; that is an attributed position, not a finding of this report.

subject: gov.protect
name: Draft organic law on personal data protection
milestone: Deposited 2025-07-14, sponsors heard 2026-02-17, the government's legal counsel and the data-protection authority heard 2026-02-25
position_end: 132 articles across six titles as deposited on 2025-07-14, introducing a data protection officer role, obliging public institutions to obtain authorisation for any processing, shifting enforcement to financial penalties through a sanctions department, and naming the press, surveillance cameras, algorithms and cross-border transfers as the uncovered domains; under committee review and not passed (2026-02)
sources: 2025-07-14-arp-tunisie-loi-organique-095-2025-protection-donnees-personnelles|2026-02-17-arp-audition-mandataires-proposition-95-2025|2026-02-25-tunisie-arp-audition-projet-loi-protection-donnees-inpdp|2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament|2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026)
note: the tabled Arabic text is held from the Assembly's own dossier for bill 095/2025, a 47-page scan whose page images have now been read directly; it would replace organic law 2004-63. The article count is settled from that text - the deputies' signed declaration sheets state 132 and the enacting text ends at article 132, both as deposited on 2025-07-14. The 123 of the February 2026 committee account reads as a transposition, the six-part structure it describes matching the tabled text section for section, and the 32 of a third account is the leading-digit loss the optical transcription makes; whether the committee has since shortened the bill is not established. The deposited text numbers two chapters four, so its six run 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6

subject: gov.protect
name: Legal basis for the linked national health dataset
note: A decree, ministerial order or data-sharing instrument stating the basis, retention rule and supervisory authority for a dataset joining health, civil-status, social-affairs and education records. The ministry asserts only that data is stored confidentially and securely.

subject: gov.protect
name: National authority for personal data protection
milestone: Cited by the replacement bill's sponsors as institutionally limited, February 2026
position_start: Constituted under the 2004 law, with no enforcement action, decision or annual report held (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged; the sponsors of the replacement bill cite its limited role as the institutional gap the bill exists to close, and it is named in none of the year's new data-concentrating systems (2026-08)

subject: gov.protect
name: Organic Law 2004-63 on personal data protection
milestone: Still the governing instrument when the replacement bill entered committee, February 2026
position_start: In force and described by civil society as unfit for the processing the state now does: it creates the data-protection authority and sets the general processing, consent and rights regime, and its chapter IV bars transfer abroad where it threatens public security or vital interests, requires an adequate level of protection in the destination country and requires the authority's prior authorisation in every case, decided within one month (2025-08)
position_end: Still the governing instrument; a 123-article replacement is in committee and has not passed (2026-08)
sources: 2004-07-27-tunisie-loi-organique-2004-63-protection-donnees-transfert|2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament|2024-04-01 Londa 2023 Digital Rights and Inclusion in Africa - Tunisia (Paradigm Initiative)
note: the primary text is now held, including the cross-border transfer chapter

subject: gov.regional
name: African Telecommunications Union council seat
milestone: Elected at the 7th Plenipotentiary Conference in Abuja, 24 July 2026
position_end: A 2027-2030 seat on the administrative council, giving a vote on continental direction across digital transformation, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and capacity building; no statement of what Tunisia intends to press for is reported (2026-07)

subject: gov.regional
name: AI Innovation and Technological Solutions Working Group chair (Arab League)
milestone: Elected chair at the Arab Permanent Committee's second inaugural meeting in Tunis, reported 1 August 2026
position_end: Chairs the Arab Permanent Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies' AI Innovation and Technological Solutions Working Group, one of six working-group chairs allocated across five Arab states at the committee's second inaugural meeting in Tunis in July 2026; no published statement of Tunisia's agenda for the seat (2026-08)
note: Exact election date not published; only "July 2026" is given.

subject: gov.regional
name: Algeria-Tunisia telecommunications cooperation
milestone: Cooperation announced, June 2026
position_end: Expanded cooperation announced across telecommunications and information technology; no instrument, amount or workplan published (2026-06)

subject: gov.regional
name: Arab Conference of Directors of Nationality and Civil Status Departments
milestone: Ninth conference closed in Tunis 2026-08-19
position_end: The ninth conference closed in Tunis with recommendations that member states expand reliance on digital identity, strengthen the legal frameworks protecting personal data in civil-status registers and share defences against cyber threats aimed at those registers; the General Secretariat of the Council of Arab Interior Ministers was asked to circulate its model framework for personal-data protection and information security in such registers and to draft a guidance manual, and Iraq's proposal for a unified Arab identity was referred to member states for study
note: recommendations only: no instrument is adopted, no member-state commitment is stated and the model framework itself is not held

subject: gov.regional
name: Arab Maghreb Union treaty
milestone: Concluded at Marrakesh, 17 February 1989
position_end: In force since 1 July 1989 with a binding judicial organ, and no summit held since 1994 - a legal frame for regional harmonisation with no active machinery behind it

subject: gov.regional
name: Triangular startup ecosystem programme with Japan
milestone: Minutes of the programme signed, reported 28 July 2026
position_end: A 2026-2028 programme convening African participants in Tunis on building startup ecosystems, with Tunisia's own Startup Act as the curriculum and the first session in December 2026 taking representatives of eight countries; the signing date is given only as recent and no amount or cost share is disclosed (2026-07)

subject: gov.standards
name: Mutual recognition of conformity certificates with Libya
milestone: Twentieth working group meeting concluded, December 2025
position_end: The two standards bodies concluded the twentieth meeting of their working group on the mutual recognition of conformity certificates and the quality and conformity marks

subject: gov.standards
name: National standardisation system and INNORPI
milestone: Public enquiry 441 opened 25 May 2026
position_start: The 2009 law founds the national standardisation system and establishes the standardisation and industrial property institute to manage standard-setting, certification and conformity marking; it was amended in 2016 and replaced a 1982 statute
position_end: The institute opened public enquiry 441, running 25 May to 24 July 2026, on draft national standards transposing the ISO measurement-management, accuracy and uncertainty-of-measurement series and cable standards
note: no count of published national standards, and no digital-specific standard, is held

subject: gov.discourse
name: Decree-Law 54 on cyber-offences and its revision
milestone: Revision bill deposited February 2024, referred to committee April 2025, no vote
position_end: The general legislation committee named revision of the 2022 cyber-offences decree-law its top priority in January 2026, with hearings planned for the journalists' union, the bar, magistrates and civil society focused on article 24; parliament's own case file records the bill deposited on 20 February 2024, referred to committee on 10 April 2025, 38 sponsors and no vote, and does not expose the operative text of the proposed amendments. In July 2026 the Sfax court of appeal handed a journalist a first firm one-year prison term, requalifying the case from the decree-law to article 86 of the telecommunications code
note: the bill's operative text is not published and is a dated absence rather than an unattempted one

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public consultation on draft policy, laws and regulations
milestone: Decree 2018-328 gazetted 6 April 2018
position_start: Consultation is required on public policies including draft legislation and regulation where a policy could directly affect stakeholders' vital interests, with stakeholders defined to include civil-society organisations, experts and economic enterprises, consultation on draft laws and decrees routed through the national legal-information portal, notice and minimum-duration rules of 15 and 5 days and 30 and 20 days for the two tracks, and a published consultation report required before adoption alongside an annual evaluation
position_end: Unchanged and still cited by ministries as the legal basis for 2026 consultations; no consultation report, annual evaluation or count of consultations run is held

subject: gov.discourse
name: World press freedom index position
position_end: 137th of 180, score 40.43 (2026), on a country entry describing a state-favoured media landscape with the 2022 cyber-offences decree-law as the principal current threat
note: a campaigning organisation's index; it is reported as a dated story about a measure, not absorbed as a finding of this report

subject: finance.budget
name: Budget allocation for the digital transition
note: An appropriation line in the 2027 finance law or the 2026 budget showing what the state spends on the digital programme. The 2027 draft names acceleration of the digital transition as a structuring axis with no allocation, target or named programme attached.

subject: finance.new
name: AfDB economic and social reforms grant
milestone: Recorded in the bank's own reporting
position_end: Closed; no evaluation or successor operation is held (2026-08)

subject: finance.new
name: EBRD loan to Tunisie Telecom
milestone: Publicly announced 16 January 2026, after board approval on 24 July 2024
position_start: Approved by the board and not announced; no drawdown on record (2025-08)
position_end: Announced at up to EUR 190m in four tranches with a first committed tranche of EUR 50m, funding a 4G-to-5G upgrade, fibre to 200,000 households, backbone and core modernisation, energy investment and the operator's connection to the submarine cable, with a complementary EUR 11m European Union grant and a first-loss guarantee (2026-01)
note: The bank's first public-sector project in Tunisia without a sovereign guarantee since 2012; interest is tied to sustainability and state-enterprise reform milestones.

subject: finance.new
name: Energy reliability, efficiency and governance programme
milestone: Financing concluded 11 November 2025; not yet effective at the June 2026 supervision report
position_end: A five-year 430 million dollar programme, including 30 million dollars of concessional climate financing, targeting 2.8 GW of new renewable capacity by 2028, an 80 per cent cost-recovery rate for the utility and a 23 per cent reduction in electricity supply costs; the lender's June 2026 supervision report records it as not yet effective
note: an energy programme rather than a digital one; it bears on the power the sector's data-centre ambitions depend on

subject: finance.new
name: EU CEF Digital grant for the Tunisian cable segment
milestone: Project period closed 31 August 2025
position_end: Closed; EUR 9.6m against a EUR 32m project budget, exactly 30%, buying the Bizerte landing station and the roughly 1,050 km Tunisian segment that Orange owns (2025-08)
note: The Commission's record states no grant-agreement signature date; a December 2022 signing carried by trade press is not supported by it.

subject: finance.new
name: Public-private partnership project development fund
milestone: Created in the first quarter of 2022 under the 2022 finance decree-law
position_end: A fund created in the first quarter of 2022 with a 15 million dinar public contribution and an expected 17 million dollars in international donations, with World Bank technical assistance, against a pipeline exceeding 4 billion dollars in proposed partnership investment across renewable energy, water, green hydrogen and a Sfax tramway
note: the 4 billion dollar figure is a proposed pipeline and not realised investment, and the international donations are unnamed

subject: finance.new
name: Sidi Bouzid II 100 MW solar independent power project
milestone: Financing closed 1 July 2026
position_end: Financing of about EUR 96 million closed on non-recourse project-finance debt from the EBRD and the EIB, an EU guarantee, a EUR 5.5 million grid-connection grant and a political-risk guarantee, against a 25-year power purchase agreement with the national utility
note: a private project financing rather than a digital-sector one; it bears on the power supply the sector's data-centre ambitions rest on

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G commercial service
milestone: All three operators launched within days of each other, February 2025
position_start: In service across all three operators since February 2025, under fifteen-year licences awarded in November 2024 (2025-08)
position_end: In service; the regulator's fixed-wireless obligation carries a 30 Mbps floor and a 50% contractual-speed guarantee, and fixed-wireless lines rose from 9,425 at launch to 319,554 by May 2026 (2026-08)
note: Independent measurement of speed is a reference study cited on this page, not absorbed as country state.

subject: infra.connect
name: Cite Numerique d'Ennahli technology park
milestone: Immediate procurement to complete the park ordered 2026-08-10
position_end: The grands projets commission ordered immediate procurement to complete the park at a review session chaired by the Prime Minister on 10 August 2026, alongside unrelated power-station and hospital projects
note: no cost, completion date, occupancy plan or account of why the park was incomplete is stated

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet use and household connection on the census series
milestone: 76.5 per cent of literate people aged 10 and over, against 40.4 per cent of households connected (2024 census)
position_end: 76.5 per cent of literate people aged 10 and over used the internet at least once in the three months before the 2024 census — 77.4 per cent of women against 75.8 per cent of men, and 81.4 per cent urban against 61 per cent rural — while 40.4 per cent of households had a home connection
note: individual use and household access are different indicators and the 36-point gap between them is the census's own

subject: infra.connect
name: Medusa submarine cable landing at Bizerte
milestone: Ready for service 3 June 2026, commercial service from 24 June
position_start: Under construction; the hosting agreement was signed in May 2023 and the cable had not landed (2025-08)
position_end: Landed 31 October 2025 as the cable's first African landing, ready for service on 3 June 2026 and carrying commercial traffic from 24 June, with Orange Tunisia owning and operating the landing station and the roughly 1,050 km Tunisian segment at up to 24 Tbps across four fibre pairs; the Marseille to Bizerte segment is co-financed 30 per cent by the European connecting facility (2026-06)
note: Both national operators' publicity claimed the landing; settled against the cable operator's own newsroom, which makes Orange the owner and Tunisie Telecom a capacity customer. Ready for service and commercial service are three weeks apart on the record and both dates are the operators' own.

subject: infra.connect
name: National fibre backbone
milestone: More than 50,000 km deployed on the incumbent's own figure, and the Medusa cable in commercial service
position_start: More than 50,000 km of fibre deployed on the incumbent operator's own statement when it won the 5G licence in November 2024, the backbone under its fibre-backed rollout
position_end: The Medusa submarine cable landed at Bizerte on 1 November 2025, the first African landing, giving the second operator up to 24 Tbps on a 1,040 km Tunisian segment, and entered commercial service on 24 June 2026 with four fibre pairs at 24 Tbps each
note: the 50,000 km figure is the operator's own and is not independently held; no national backbone map or fibre-route inventory is published

subject: infra.connect
name: Regulated access to the submarine cable landing station
milestone: Regulator decision 165-2013 of 15 November 2013
position_end: The regulator requires cost-oriented, regulated third-party access to the incumbent's submarine-cable landing station, a decision taken after access terms proved prohibitive enough that an alternative cable was built to bypass it
note: no later access decision, tariff or dispute is held, and nothing states whether the 2013 decision has been applied to the newer cable

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite service licence
milestone: Pre-orders opened February 2026 with no licence issued
position_start: Application pending since January 2023, with technical trials run in 2023 and no licence (2025-08)
position_end: Still unlicensed after three years; the operator opened US$9 refundable pre-order deposits in February 2026, and a March 2025 feasibility study recommended a time-limited competitive licence, deferred to let 5G and fibre consolidate (2026-06)
note: The unresolved point is routing: the state wants low-earth-orbit traffic through a local ground station and a national interconnection point.

subject: infra.connect
name: Telecommunications sector observatory series
milestone: Mobile-data subscriptions 10.9 million in 2025, fixed data traffic 7,512 petabytes
position_start: Sector revenue up 3.3 per cent year on year to 1.075 billion dinars in the third quarter of 2025, 69 per cent of it from data services, mobile-data penetration at 93.9 per cent and fixed household internet penetration at 51 per cent on denominators recalculated after the 2024 census, with fixed data traffic up from 1,555 to 1,989 petabytes
position_end: Mobile-data subscriptions up 2.8 per cent to 10.9 million over 2025 and fixed-data subscriptions up 7.3 per cent, annual traffic reaching 1,224 petabytes on mobile and 7,512 on fixed networks, with fixed wireless access consumption up 115 per cent
note: the regulator's own series; the annual report carries no exact publication day

subject: infra.connect
name: Tunisie Telecom dedicated Medusa fibre pair
milestone: In service with the cable, 3 June 2026
position_start: Contracted at 20 Tbps in February 2025, not in service (2025-08)
position_end: In service on the operational cable; the operator's claim of an eightfold capacity increase is about its own purchased capacity, not the cable (2026-06)
note: The cable operator's record gives the pair as 20 Tbps; trade press and a national news re-report give 22 Tbps.

subject: infra.connect
name: TUNIXP national internet exchange point
milestone: Operated by the internet agency, which has run internet infrastructure since 1996
position_end: The Tunisian internet agency operates and manages the national internet exchange point, alongside message gateways for service providers, the country-code domain registry in Latin and Arabic script, and national address allocation
note: the agency's own institutional page, undated; no founding decree, member list, peering count or traffic figure for the exchange is held

subject: infra.store
name: Centre National de Backup
milestone: Initiated 2006 with World Bank support; the state's recovery site for critical applications
position_start: The recovery site for critical state applications, with a standards-compliant data centre, a redundant fibre backbone and round-the-clock on-site security
position_end: Unchanged on the operator's own account; no capacity, tested-recovery time or list of applications covered is published
note: the page carries a 2016 copyright as its only dateline and remains the operator's current statement

subject: infra.store
name: Data centres as a state investment priority
milestone: Carried as a named project line in the development plan annex, June 2026
position_start: Named one of two core priorities at the Investment Authority's 22nd Strategic Council, with recommendations to modernise data-protection law, expand renewables and create a cloud special economic zone (2025-10)
position_end: Carried as a named project line in the statutory development plan alongside artificial intelligence and digitalisation, with no budget line, no sequencing and no delivery agency stated (2026-06)
note: the investment authority's own announcement of the October 2025 session is now held, presenting data centres as a priority sector and positioning the country as a regional hosting hub tied to digital sovereignty

subject: infra.store
name: Private cloud for the national computing centre
milestone: Contract awarded, 24-month build from 2 February 2026
position_end: An African Development Bank-financed contract for a private cloud for the state computing centre was awarded to a Tunisian and Chinese consortium at about EUR 8.17 million including tax, on a 24-month build starting 2 February 2026, modernising the national hosting platform alongside the existing backup centre
note: an award rather than a delivery; no capacity, tenancy model or migration plan is stated

subject: infra.store
name: SoleCrypt Bizerte data centre
milestone: Non-binding memorandum with Schneider Electric, February 2026
position_end: A 20 MW artificial-intelligence data centre planned at the landing point of three subsea cables, to be powered from the developer's own 60 MW solar site; the memorandum is non-binding and no financing, permit or construction start is published (2026-02)

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign cloud for national health data
milestone: Health ministry confirmed an intention to adopt Tunisian cloud solutions, February 2026
position_end: A stated intention to host national health data on Tunisian cloud solutions, with no amount, date, named agreement or provider (2026-02)
sources: 2026-02-13 Tunisia Advances Digital Health Reform With AI and National Cloud Strategy

subject: infra.store
name: State bank data-centre and recovery-site extension
milestone: Tender awarded 29 June 2026 at 6.03 million dinars
position_end: A state bank awarded a two-lot tender worth 6,029,732 dinars including tax for extension of server and storage infrastructure at both its principal and its backup data centres
note: a single institution's procurement; it is the only dated off-site recovery capacity outside the state computing centre on this ledger

subject: infra.energy
name: Grid reliability and distribution losses
milestone: Average interruption duration 108 minutes at end-2025, ahead of target
position_start: Average interruption duration 137 minutes at the December 2023 baseline, with distribution losses at 18.40 per cent
position_end: 108 minutes at 31 December 2025, ahead of the 133 to 135 minute target for the year, while losses worsened to 19 per cent
note: the lender's own supervision report; reliability improved and losses did not, which is why the two are reported together

subject: infra.energy
name: Renewable power for data-centre capacity
milestone: Developer's Tozeur solar site at base-camp stage, November 2025
position_end: A 60 MW solar site is to power the planned Bizerte facility, its base camp operational from November 2025; no grid connection or power purchase arrangement is published (2026-02)

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural electrification rate
milestone: 97.0 per cent of rural dwellings connected at the 2024 census
position_end: 97.0 per cent of rural dwellings connected to the grid against 97.9 per cent urban and 97.7 per cent nationally, with photovoltaic lighting reaching only 1.4 per cent of rural dwellings
note: the census's own figures; near-universal grid connection and negligible off-grid solar are two findings, not one

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural grid extension and off-grid installer accreditation
milestone: 20 firms on the June 2026 accreditation registry
position_end: The utility tendered grid extension for three zones of the Tataouine governorate with bids due in January 2026, and the energy agency's June 2026 registry lists 20 firms accredited to install photovoltaic systems for rural electrification and public lighting
note: a tender and a registry are the delivery machinery; no programme budget, target or connection series is held

subject: infra.capacity
name: Centre National de l'Informatique
milestone: Founded by law 75-83 of 30 December 1975, missions set by decree 2007-1359
position_start: The state computing centre, founded in 1975, with managed operation of national systems, e-administration and information-technology training for the administration in its statutory remit
position_end: Unchanged; it is also the sole interoperability operator designated by the 2020 decree-law, and no staffing, skills or operations figure for it is published
note: the institution's own history page; nothing states how many people run the national platforms it operates

subject: infra.capacity
name: Domestic technical capacity to operate the national digital estate
note: A staffing plan, skills audit or operations report covering who runs the interoperability platform, the identity layer and the health identifier.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Circular requiring a common security baseline for public digital systems
milestone: Circular n. 5 issued 2 September 2026
position_end: The head of government issued circular n. 5 on 2 September 2026 setting a security baseline across official websites, public service platforms and state messaging: encrypted connections generalised, security certificates renewed on a mandatory cycle, two-factor verification for administrator access, protection against traffic-saturation attacks, and an obligation to host data on servers approved by the state. It bans the use of WhatsApp and social media for exchanging official documents, requires regular audits, immediate reporting of incidents to the national cybersecurity agency and an end to the sharing of credentials between colleagues; it sits in a line running from the 2023 cybersecurity decree
note: a circular binds the administration rather than the wider economy, and no compliance deadline, audit schedule, budget or list of state-approved hosting providers is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity agency
milestone: Public advisory on an SMS phishing campaign, 30 July 2026
position_start: Created by the 2023 cybersecurity decree-law as successor to the information security agency established in 2004, with the hosting label regime in its remit
position_end: Issuing public advisories against a live campaign harvesting banking and personal data; its offered verification test is that Tunisian government sites use only the .tn domain, and no takedown power, enforcement action or role for the data-protection authority is on record (2026-07)
note: the founding decree-law is now held; the agency's advisory notices are the only activity on the record, and no takedown power, enforcement action or role for the data-protection authority appears in it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Recorded cyberattacks and ransomware cases
milestone: Interior ministry and agency figures reported 2026-08-07
position_end: 57,430 cyberattacks recorded in the first half of 2025, and ransomware cases up 140% to 37,076 in 2024, on interior ministry and national security agency figures, as the government finalised a National Cybersecurity Strategy 2026-2030 aimed at critical-infrastructure resilience and skills
note: the two figures cover different periods and are not a series; no definition of a recorded attack, and no incident-reporting obligation behind the count, is stated

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Data exchange between the social schemes, health and the national computing centre
milestone: Sector interoperability services listed complete at end-2025
position_start: A framework agreement between the ministries of social affairs and health and the national computing centre, with over 6 million health-insurance data-exchange operations across 92 health facilities on the Labes card
position_end: The Council of Ministers listed interoperability services for the social-affairs sector among the digital-transformation projects completed by the end of 2025, alongside phase one of the national interconnection platform
note: the completion claim is the council's own; no service list, volume or scheme coverage is published behind it

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Electronic rules-of-origin system
milestone: Execution phase opened, technical preparation running to 2026-09-18
position_end: An integrated electronic rules-of-origin system for the customs administration, financed by a bilateral partner, with its execution phase opened and technical preparation running to 18 September 2026
note: no go-live date, trader-facing interface or cost is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Hospital information systems and the computerised medical record
milestone: Loan amendment approved by parliament 12 February 2026, drawdown extended to 2028
movement: Advanced, on financing rather than deployment
position_start: Largely paper-based: the computerised medical record pilot faces connectivity and functionality problems, is fully installed in 50 per cent of university hospitals and 32 per cent of regional hospitals, is absent from district hospitals and basic health centres, there is no unified chronic-disease registry, and the emergency service runs on paper reports that do not integrate with hospital records
position_end: Parliament approved by 94 votes to 2 with 3 abstentions the second amendment to the 2019 development-agency loan financing the e-health programme, EUR 27.3 million for information systems across 24 university hospitals, five regional telemedicine initiatives and institutional strengthening, with the drawdown deadline extended to 30 September 2028 and only about 16 per cent drawn
note: the financing moved; no later deployment figure supersedes the 2025 installation percentages

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National interoperability platform (UXP)
milestone: Phase 2 contract signed, May 2026
position_start: Phase 1 live as a proof of concept across five ministries, with a central governing authority established (2025-08)
position_end: Phase 2 contracted, extending the platform to the business register, the investment authority, the industry and export promotion agencies, the finance ministry and the central bank; completion 2027 (2026-05)
sources: 2026-05-14-cybernetica-national-interoperability-platform-phase2|2024-02-14 National interoperability platform in Tunisia (Cybernetica UXP)

subject: dpi.id
name: Digital consular civil-status services
milestone: Directed by restricted Council of Ministers, 25 April 2026
position_end: A restricted Council of Ministers directed development of digital consular services including remote extraction of civil-status documents and remote registration of births, deaths and marriages abroad, and completion of the digital consular portal
note: a direction with no timetable, budget or delivery date attached

subject: dpi.id
name: e-Houwiya mobile identity
milestone: Made compulsory for business registration and investment declarations from 1 July 2026
position_start: Live and voluntary, at 200,000 subscribers as of March 2025, with no legal obligation to hold one (2025-08)
position_end: Compulsory from 1 July 2026 for access to the business register — Mobile ID for natural persons and DigiGO for legal persons — and for agricultural investment declarations at the investment promotion agency; no subscriber figure has been published since March 2025 (2026-07)
sources: 2026-04-30-tunisie-rne-full-digital-mobile-id|2026-06-30-tunisie-apia-hoyia-raqmiya-mobile-id-investissement|2026-06-26-techafricanews-mobile-id-mandatory-investors|2026-04-27-africanmanager-national-business-register-digital|2025-03-19 E-Houwiya - A Milestone in Tunisia's Digital Transformation Roadmap 2025 (ID Tech)
note: Two independent public-service rails switched to compulsory digital identity on the same date, and a second credential type for legal persons appears alongside the citizen one.

subject: dpi.id
name: Identifiant Social Unique (social identifier system)
milestone: Ministerial working session at La Kasbah, 18 August 2026
position_end: Government decided at a ministerial session on 18 August 2026 to upgrade the social identifier system, digitise social-security cards and services, process claims instantaneously and put interconnected systems in place for real-time data exchange between the social funds, health structures and insured persons, with drafting of the structural-reform texts to begin immediately. No drafting timetable, legal basis for the identifier or scope definition is stated
note: the government's own communique, posted 2026-08-19 for a session held 18 August 2026; the digital leg sits inside the health half of a wider social-security reform decision

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity and travel documents issued through digital services
milestone: Interior ministry figures as at 2026-08-18
position_end: Mobile electronic counters aboard two ferries issued several thousand passports at sea to the returning diaspora, and expatriate-support offices on national territory issued 10,609 official documents
note: a ministry statement rather than a published series; the passport figure is given as several thousand without a number

subject: dpi.id
name: Issuance of the biometric identity card and passport
sources: 2024-04-23 Tunisia - Biometric ID card and passport usage to begin in H1 2025|2024-03-07 Eight years in the making - Tunisia's Biometric ID and Passport Bills risk rights
note: An interior ministry statement, an issuance figure or a gazette notice. The enabling organic laws passed in March 2024 and use was targeted for the first half of 2025; nothing held states whether issuance has begun.

subject: dpi.id
name: National Health Identifier
milestone: Adopted by health institutions in Kebili from July 2026, beyond the university-hospital pilot
position_end: Health institutions in the interior region of Kebili began adopting it in July 2026, linking each patient file to the national identity number for registration and inter-facility exchange, after a university-hospital pilot from June 2026; over 15,000 numbers issued as at 22 June and roughly 100,000 medical files linked as at 27 July 2026 (2026-07)
note: Three counts circulate at three scopes and do not contradict each other; no national coverage figure has been published by the ministry, and no public dashboard exists.

subject: dpi.id
name: Registre de l'identifiant unique citoyen
milestone: Created by decree-law 2020-17 of 12 May 2020, with its register rules set three days later
position_start: A register held and managed by the ministry of local affairs, assigning a unique identifier to every Tunisian registered in the civil-status birth register including births registered abroad through diplomatic and consular missions, with the data-protection authority's opinion required before the technical specification and usage rules are set
position_end: Unchanged in law; the implementing decree fixing the identifier's content, technical specification and register rules followed on 15 May 2020
note: no issuance figure, coverage rate or birth-registration linkage measure is held

subject: dpi.id
name: Unified national population registry
milestone: 72 municipalities trained on civil-registration harmonisation, November to December 2025
position_start: An objective and not an institution: a July 2025 national workshop with the statistics institute and the interior ministry mapped the legal and regulatory revision a unified registry would need
position_end: Three training workshops run by the interior ministry, the statistics institute and the national computing centre covered 72 municipalities and harmonised civil-registration and vital-statistics practice, including the Medania digital system
note: the registry itself remains unbuilt; no legal instrument, timetable or coverage target is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Accession to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System
milestone: Acceded 6 February 2024
position_end: The central bank acceded to the pan-African payment and settlement system on 6 February 2024 under the continental free trade area framework, with banks and the post office required to obtain a non-objection attestation before participating directly
note: no transaction volume, participating-bank count or corridor is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Active digital wallet count
sources: 2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025
note: The central bank's own payments bulletin. The wiki carries 815,000 for 2025 from an aggregator; reporting attributed directly to the bulletins gives roughly 469,000 at end-2025, a divergence of about a factor of 1.7, and only the aggregator's side is held.

subject: dpi.pay
name: AMEN Social monthly allowance
milestone: Raised from 260 to 280 dinars, retroactive to January 2026
position_end: 280 dinars a month for poor households, retroactive to January 2026, by joint order gazetted 7 August 2026

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic payment of AMEN Social transfers
milestone: Target of 300,000 beneficiaries on electronic payment deferred to 2029
movement: Stalled, the electronic-payment target moved out to 2029
position_start: Digitalisation and interoperability of the transfer payment process, under a World Bank operation
position_end: The performance target of 300,000 beneficiaries receiving transfers through electronic payment methods is now scheduled for 2029
note: no current count of beneficiaries paid electronically is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic payment of customs duties
milestone: Decree 2024-463 gazetted 23 August 2024
position_end: A decree setting the rules for electronic payment of customs duties, taxes and penalties to the Treasury through the integrated automated foreign-trade formalities system, settling to the Treasury's current account at the central bank
note: no share of duties paid electronically is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Family allowance for children aged 6 to 18
milestone: First tranche disbursed 11 December 2025
position_end: The first tranche of the allowance created by government decree 2025-426 of 2 October 2025 was disbursed on 11 December 2025, covering the first half of 2025
note: how the payment reaches beneficiaries, and what share of it is electronic, is not stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: Free digital wallets for university registration
milestone: Offered 2026-08-31
position_end: the postal operator providing digital wallets free to students for the 2026-2027 university registration

subject: dpi.pay
name: Honour loans moved fully online
milestone: Decree 2026-148 of 23 July 2026 fixing the conditions and criteria
position_end: Banks have moved honour-loan applications to a wholly online process, stated as ending queueing at branches; no volume, approval rate or processing time is on file
note: the founding instrument is now held: Decree 2026-148 of 23 July 2026, published in the official journal, fixes the conditions and criteria for granting the honour micro-financings the secondary account described by its ceilings and grace period alone

subject: dpi.pay
name: Kashy wallet (Tunisie Telecom)
milestone: Launched by the state operator, March 2026
position_end: Launched with a licensed payment partner, offering transfers, collections, top-up and cash withdrawal by phone (2026-03)
note: The wiki's capture of the only source no longer carries the article; the publisher redirects the identifier to its homepage, so the launch detail is not currently citable beyond the headline.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Licensed payment institutions
milestone: 16 licensed after a definitive authorisation of 29 January 2026
position_end: 16 licensed payment institutions after the central bank's licensing commission granted definitive resident authorisation to a Qatari-owned fintech subsidiary by decision of 29 January 2026, gazetted, with six months to begin operating
note: this count and the 435 payment service providers reported for 2025 are different populations under different definitions, and no source reconciles them

subject: dpi.pay
name: Licensed payment service providers
milestone: Central bank full-year figures for 2025, reported February 2026
sources: 2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025

subject: dpi.pay
name: Loss-allocation rule for compromised electronic payments
milestone: Absence set out in a published legal analysis, 2026-08-09
position_end: Not held
note: a published analysis finds no Tunisian text - not the 2000 electronic commerce law, the 2023 cybersecurity decree-law or the central bank's 2024 circular - allocating the loss between bank, merchant and cardholder when an electronic payment is hijacked, altered or blocked by a cyber incident, against a payments market of 164.8 million transactions worth 29.5bn dinars in 2025, up 12.3%, and reported cyber incidents rising from 63,000 in 2021 to more than 155,000 in 2022

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile payment transactions
milestone: Central bank full-year figures for 2025, reported February 2026
position_end: 8.4m transactions worth TND 1,769m in 2025, up 81% year on year, with peer-to-peer transfers 50.7% of operations and merchant payments 17.8% (2025)
sources: 2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025
note: The central bank's own payments bulletin is not held; these figures reach the wiki through an aggregator's repackaging.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Remote filing of foreign-exchange authorisations
milestone: Central bank circular 2025-12 of 9 October 2025
position_end: A central bank circular moving the filing of foreign-exchange authorisations onto a secure portal and phasing out paper filing during 2026
note: no filing volume or completion date for the paper phase-out is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: SIBTEL clearing, the SMT card system and the SGMT settlement system
milestone: The settlement system in service since November 2006, moving about 722 payments a day worth 3.255 billion dinars
position_start: The central bank's own account of the national rails: SIBTEL clearing for transfers under 100 thousand dinars, direct debits, cheques and bills of exchange settling in 24 hours, the SMT card system with its secure online payment service, and the SGMT real-time gross settlement system in service since November 2006
position_end: Unchanged; about 722 payments a day worth 3.255 billion dinars pass through the settlement system on the central bank's own figures
note: the page carries no publication date of its own and the figures are the central bank's

subject: dpi.pay
name: TUNPAY national payment label
milestone: Created by central bank note 2026-132 of 5 May 2026
position_end: A single national label for mobile payment, created by the central bank with the national card and mobile-payment operator as switch operator, which banks, payment institutions and the postal service must adopt across their networks, wallet applications, interfaces and acceptance points including merchants and agents (2026-05)
note: the primary instrument is now held, signed by the governor and carrying the annexed label prototype

subject: dpi.pay
name: walletii (Ooredoo Fintech)
milestone: Central bank licence awarded, March 2026
position_end: Licensed with a Gulf banking group and the national payments operator, targeting the underbanked over an agent network; no launch date or user figure published (2026-03)

subject: dpi.registry
name: AMEN social registry
milestone: Over 333,000 households on cash transfers as of December 2023
position_start: Over 333,000 poor households on monthly cash transfers and over 620,000 low-income households on free or subsidised healthcare, with 44.4% of cash transfers digitalised (2023-12)
position_end: Unchanged on coverage; the founding organic law of January 2019 requires the register to cover demographic, health, education, social, economic and service data on poor and low-income households, to be updated at least every two years, and obliges public data-holding bodies to feed it (2026-08)
sources: 2019-01-30-tunisie-loi-organique-2019-10-amen-social|2024-11-14 Tunisians Share How their Life Changed Through the AMEN Program|2020-01-01 Nexus between Civil Registration and Social Protection - Tunisia chapter (IDRC)
note: the founding statute is now held; no coverage or digitalisation update has been published since December 2023

subject: dpi.registry
name: Digital birth declaration platform
milestone: Remote issuance launched 2026-08-31
position_end: birth certificates issued remotely through the national services platform, with a remote translation service alongside

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land-registry request processing time
milestone: Average processing cut from 40 days to 8
position_start: 40 days on average to process a registration request
position_end: 8 days, with the second-generation land-registry data-processing system networked across all 22 regional directorates and about 120,000 online service requests received since March 2022
note: the office's own figures, given by its chief executive to the state news agency

subject: dpi.registry
name: Livre foncier and compulsory land registration
milestone: Compulsory registration opened in six governorates from 1 November 2026
position_start: Compulsory land registration runs under a 1964 decree-law dividing roles between the land tribunal, the survey and cadastre office for surveying and plans, and the national land property office for inscription on the livre foncier
position_end: Six ministerial decisions gazetted in August 2026 open compulsory cadastral survey and registration of unregistered unbuilt property, from 1 November 2026, in named zones of the Kasserine, Mahdia, Jendouba, Medenine, Sfax and Gabes governorates
note: no figure for the share of national territory registered is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Business Register digitalisation
milestone: Digital identity made the mandatory authentication key from 1 July 2026, with an electronic safe from 1 September
position_end: From 1 July 2026 all procedures move online only, with the national digital identity as the mandatory authentication key — Mobile ID for natural persons and DigiGO for legal persons — and from 1 September 2026 an electronic safe account keyed to the enterprise unique identifier; a February 2026 ministerial order tasks the register with hosting the remote company-declaration platform and mandates an electronic tax identity card sealed by the certification agency and issued within one working day (2026-04)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Register of electors
milestone: Held under organic law 2012-23, as modified by decree-law 2022-22
position_start: The electoral authority holds and permanently updates the register of electors and finalises and publishes the electoral lists for each election, under its founding organic law of December 2012 as modified in April 2022
position_end: Unchanged on the record; no registration count, update cycle or audit of the register is held
note: the record's staged publication date is unsupported by its own captured body and is kept as staged rather than guessed at

subject: dpi.registry
name: Social housing digital application platform
milestone: Completion timetable set at a follow-up meeting, 3 August 2026, with beneficiary-database interconnection still under way
position_end: A single platform for rent-to-own and instalment-sale applications for social housing; the ministry set a completion timetable and called for regional officials to be trained before rollout, with beneficiary-database interconnection - led with the national computing centre - still facing technical and administrative obstacles; no launch date, budget or application volume published (2026-08)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Tax identifier and the TEJ filing platform
milestone: Tax-file and transfer-pricing filings made exclusively electronic, March 2026
position_start: The tax identifier is granted by the territorially competent tax-control office after a declaration of existence, under article 56 of the income and corporate tax code and a 2008 decree
position_end: The tax administration made filing of the tax file and transfer-pricing declarations exclusively electronic through its TEJ platform, and required taxpayers to regularise omitted filings and update legal-representative identity data on it
note: the tax administration's own communique was not found at a stable address; the change is held on the fullest dated report of it

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital hospital project
milestone: Carried as a plan project with telemedicine and imaging first
position_end: Phase 1 reported delivered by end-2025 and the project carried in the statutory development plan; no facility count, budget or completion date published (2026-06)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital hospital remote examinations
milestone: 120,000 remote examinations reported across 26 hospitals
position_start: Did not exist as a reported total
position_end: 120,000 remote examinations carried out across 26 hospitals under the digital hospital programme
note: A cumulative total with no start date given, so the rate cannot be read from it.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digitisation of the state property inventory
milestone: 10,000 of 52,600 properties inventoried
movement: Advanced, the total the project must cover is now stated
position_start: Over 10,000 state properties digitised into a unified database with the survey and cadastre office and the national remote-sensing centre, and a priority state-property registration project budgeted at 900,000 dinars (2025-11)
position_end: 10,000 of 52,600 state-owned properties inventoried on the minister's account to parliament, launched after a general survey proved unsatisfactory — the first statement of the total to be covered (2026-04)
note: the minister's own figures; no completion date is held, and the count has not moved between the two statements

subject: dpi.mis
name: Electronic exchange of judicial documents and remote hearings
milestone: First fully paperless administrative hearing at Gabes, February 2026
position_start: Real experimental operation from 21 November 2024 of electronic judicial-document exchange for civil matters, with the country's first interactive remote hearings, at the model Ben Arous court of first instance under the 2023-2025 judicial digital-transition programme
position_end: The Gabes regional chamber of the administrative court held a fully paperless hearing under an integrated system live there since 29 December 2025 covering first-instance, referral, stay-of-execution and legal-aid cases, and the justice minister chaired an April 2026 session pressing for completion of the integrated penal and civil justice system and the judges' case-management platform
note: two separate systems are in play, the justice ministry's civil-court pilot and the administrative court's own; nothing states how they relate or how many courts either reaches

subject: dpi.mis
name: Office of Trade stock and sales management application
milestone: Presented at a working session, reported 2026-09-01
position_end: An application built in-house by the Tunisian Office of Trade's IT department to manage human resources and the supply chain, in particular stocks and sales, tracking the office's performance indicators and the movement of storage and distribution centres including available stock, and following the regularity of sale procedures for internal control; purchasing and logistics are to be added later, with a user guide to follow
note: the office is a public enterprise; no launch date, cost or coverage figure is published and the application had not gone live at the date of the account

subject: dpi.mis
name: Sahetna.tn health portal
milestone: In final technical configuration, July 2026
position_end: In final technical configuration and not launched, built on the generalisation of the national health identifier across public health structures and university hospitals, with a shared unified medical record to move clinical data between emergency departments and operating theatres and joint technical commissions to extend both the identifier and the portal to private clinics and laboratories; no legal basis, retention rule or data-protection authority is named for the linked dataset (2026-07)

subject: dpi.mis
name: School life platform (viescolaire.education.tn)
milestone: 53 per cent of pupils enrolled online for 2026/2027 by 20 August 2026
position_end: A unified portal launched at the end of July 2026 linking a citizen account to the student record, with 53 per cent of pupils enrolled for the 2026/2027 year by 20 August; families reported the enrolment period as an ordeal, and no outage log, completion rate or ministry response is on file
note: a service that exists and does not work is a different finding from one that does not exist; the platform's legal basis, its data-protection basis, retention rule and pupil-record scope, and its relationship to tarbia.tn are not stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Tunisian Land Information System (TLIS)
milestone: Under execution in the survey office's 2020-2025 programme
position_end: A project to digitise the survey office's activity and technical archive, described by the equipment and housing ministry's own working session as under execution and not yet operational
note: no completion date, budget or coverage figure is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Centre Informatique du Ministere de l'Interieur
milestone: Created by decree 2016-566 of 2 May 2016
position_start: The interior ministry's information-systems body, with strategy, hosting, data-bank administration and electronic services in its remit
position_end: Unchanged in law; it is the body behind the ministry's identity, civil-status and municipal permit systems
note: no source names a station-level or rural-specific digitisation act, so this is the closest institutional anchor for one

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital service houses
milestone: 34 completed across 21 governorates between December 2025 and June 2026
position_end: 34 completed across 21 governorates between December 2025 and June 2026, reaching more than 900,000 citizens, with unserved areas including Hrairia and El Ouardia deferred to a 2027-2030 successor programme
note: the reach figure is the programme's own and counts citizens reached rather than transactions completed; no service list or staffing model is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital-transformation projects in execution
milestone: 114 projects in execution at the 2026-08-16 council; 192 under national tracking on the government's own communique of 2026-08-17
position_start: A 2025-2026 digital transformation programme of 138 projects, including 12 on national cyberspace protection and digital trust, reviewed by the Council of Ministers in September 2025
position_end: 114 projects in execution, some reported above 90% complete, covering remote residence certificates, driving-licence renewal, remote passport and identity-card applications, the national health identifier and customs and health-insurance systems; the government's own communique of 2026-08-17 puts 192 projects under national tracking, naming a national interconnection platform and the Easy Export and Nationalite systems, within a 2026-2030 unified national digital-transformation vision
note: three counts are now on the record — 138 in the 2025-2026 programme, 114 in execution and 192 under national tracking — measured differently and nowhere reconciled, with no project list or completion series published for any of them

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-industrie unified platform
milestone: In service 2026-08-28
position_end: a unified platform brought into service as the single digital gateway to the industry, mines and energy ministry's services

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Education platform (tarbia.tn)
milestone: Launched by the education ministry, January 2024
position_start: Live since January 2024; the target of connecting 3,300 schools to broadband by end-2024 had no published outcome (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged; the broadband target still has no published outcome (2026-08)
sources: 2024-01-08 Tunisia Unveils Digital Platform to Boost Education Transparency, Equity

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Industry ministry unified digital services platform
milestone: Platform opened 2026-08-28
position_end: Opened at e-industrie.gov.tn with its first online service, the technical cards governing effective transfer operations of which the ministry processes more than 4,000 a year, filed and processed entirely online and interconnected with the customs administration so that data is exchanged and decisions notified in real time; import authorisations under terms-of-reference regimes, the packaged olive oil promotion fund and class 1 and 2 establishment licences follow on a phased timetable
note: the platform runs on the MobileID and Digigo digital identity mechanisms and is linked to the Registre National des Entreprises

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Khadamet mobile portal for administrative services
milestone: First version launched 31 August 2026 and presented publicly on 2 September
position_end: A Mobile ID-authenticated application giving unified access to administrative procedures — civil status, health insurance and social-security career and contribution data, tax, vehicles, bills and enrolments — so a user can follow their own files. A ministry official said about 70 per cent of citizens reach services by mobile phone, which is why the ministry built a mobile gateway rather than another web portal
note: it sits on top of the existing khadamet.gov.tn administrative portal rather than replacing it, and a commentary published on launch day put the test where it belongs: the promise is aggregation, and its worth depends on whether the administrations behind it keep their service commitments; no service count, user figure or transaction volume is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National register of community companies
milestone: Launched at alahlia.tn, 20 July 2026, under decree-law n 3 of 2025
position_end: Live, covering formation, filings and tracking of ministry responses; the launch disclosed 230 companies created, 15,000 participants, 60 operational and 380 jobs, with personal-data storage described as secure and no legal basis, retention rule or regulator named (2026-07)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online business tax registration
milestone: Platform deployed by the tax directorate, announced 4 August 2026
position_start: Did not exist; the declaration of existence required a visit to a tax office
position_end: Filed remotely with real-time tracking, correction of the tax file and download of the tax identification card, available at all hours; announced by video capsule rather than by gazette, and the confidentiality assurance names neither an instrument nor a supervisory authority (2026-08)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Single administrative services portal
milestone: Reported delivered by end-2025 in the ministerial council's account
position_end: Reported delivered among a portfolio of 192 tracked projects, alongside remote vehicle-tax payment, the electronic fiscal stamp, a building-permit platform and a citizenship system; no usage figure is published for any of them (2026-02)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Wholesale-markets e-invoicing and traceability programme (SOTUMAG)
milestone: Pilot completed at the Moknine wholesale market; official launch at Teboulba set for 15 August 2026
position_end: Piloted successfully at the Moknine fruit-and-vegetable wholesale market under the Ministry of Trade and Export Development; official launch at the Teboulba wholesale market set for 15 August 2026 alongside sanitary certification and a produce-traceability system, with further extension planned to the Kairouan and Gabes national-interest markets (2026-08)
note: A sector programme run through the state wholesale-markets company under the trade ministry; its relationship, if any, to the Article 53 compulsory e-invoicing amendment under separate committee review is not stated in either source.

subject: digital.localgov
name: REMO local digital governance project
milestone: Closed 30 April 2026 after four years
position_end: Closed on 30 April 2026, leaving digital service houses in 19 communes, three Espaces Citoyens and four solutions including the GRB 2.0 municipal revenue-management system, the MSA platform, Tabbaa and Tathmine
note: a German development agency and interior ministry project; how its 19 communes relate to the national digital service house count is not stated

subject: digital.localgov
name: Taamir building-permit platform
milestone: First fully online permit issued 24 June 2026
position_end: The municipality of Tunis issued the first fully online building permit on 24 June 2026, with the national platform generalised to 16 municipalities under the interior ministry's computing centre
note: no rollout schedule and no permit volume is held

subject: digital.rural
name: Ecoles Numeriques digital-education kits
milestone: 185 primary schools equipped since 2014
position_start: 185 public primary schools equipped with offline-capable digital-education kits since 2014, with the education ministry and the national education technology centre
position_end: 15 further schools announced for the 2025-2026 year on top of the 185, with a first extension of the kit model into three public hospitals
note: the two records do not reconcile: 15 schools were announced on top of 185 in September 2025, and the foundation's own programme page still read 185 a year later

subject: digital.rural
name: Edunet 10 school connectivity
milestone: Most schools connected, on the minister's statement of 3 November 2025
position_end: Most schools connected to high-speed internet and equipped with computer laboratories, on the education minister's own account, framed as equity between all regions
note: the minister's own claim; no school-level count, no definition of most and no rural breakdown is held

subject: digital.rural
name: Model police and national guard centres
milestone: 21 centres announced, 10 national guard and 11 national security
position_end: 21 model centres under construction separating administrative from judicial offices, with digital fingerprint readers progressively replacing ink, an SMS remote-appointment system, and online identity-card and civil-status services
note: where the 21 sit and whether any is rural is not stated

subject: digital.rural
name: SI-SSPL primary-care information system
milestone: Deployed on Nabeul pilot sites
position_end: An EU and health-ministry programme covering diagnosis, governance, a national computerised medical record and deployment on pilot sites in Nabeul, that is on first-line care including basic health centres
note: the programme's own results page, which carries no publication date of its own

subject: digital.rural
name: Vaccine cold-chain management platform
milestone: In operation since 2025 across 500 sites
position_end: In operation since 2025 across 500 health centres and local hospitals, on the health ministry's written reply to parliament, which also put a national health identifier and digitised school and university medical records at 2026
note: the ministry's own figure to parliament; no site list and no uptime or stock-out measure is held

subject: tech.ai
name: GAINAfrica generative-AI agriculture pilot
milestone: Pilot running under a Horizon Europe project across five African countries
position_end: Crop-disease and precision-agriculture tools are being piloted under GAINAfrica, a Horizon Europe project led by La Sapienza in Rome; no user count, evaluation or end date is on file

subject: tech.ai
name: Livre Blanc on artificial intelligence for Tunisia
milestone: Published open source by a diaspora association and presented at the Tunisia Global Forum
position_end: A 2030 vision authored by an association and offered to the state for debate, naming the absence of large-scale data centres and sovereign compute, brain drain and under-equipped small firms as the constraints, and prescribing frugal compute investment sized by measured demand; declared open source but not posted anywhere reachable, so its content is held at press-summary precision (2026-08)

subject: tech.ai
name: Machine-learning electricity demand forecasting
milestone: Presented as a closing result of the grid decarbonisation project, June 2026
position_end: The utility and the Japanese cooperation agency presented an automated machine-learning electricity demand forecasting system as a closing result of the grid decarbonisation project, moving a core network-management function onto machine learning
note: no accuracy figure against the forecasting method it replaces is given

subject: tech.ai
name: Machine-learning module in the customs selectivity system
milestone: Integrated by customs communique of 16 May 2026
position_end: Customs formally integrated a machine-learning module into the national selectivity system for risk targeting of customs declarations
note: no accuracy, inspection-rate or appeal statistic is published, and no statement of how a targeting decision can be contested

subject: tech.ai
name: National artificial intelligence strategy
milestone: Outlines presented to a restricted ministerial council 2026-08-16; critique published 2026-08-17
position_start: A four-axis strategy described by the communication technologies minister in May 2026, covering health, agriculture and digital sovereignty, with legal and regulatory frameworks for responsible use in drafting as its governance pillar and no text published (2026-05)
position_end: A National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030 exists in outline, presented to a restricted ministerial council by the communication technologies minister and framed around Tunisia's ranking in the world's top 30, at 29th, for scientific publications on artificial intelligence; no adopted text, cabinet decision, budget or roadmap is published. A published critique finds the strategy long on ambition and short on budget, timeline and data-governance detail, and questions whether its digital-sovereignty framing stands in for independent oversight
note: the publications ranking is a research-output measure and is not evidence of state capability; the strategy text itself is not held

subject: tech.industry
name: Foreign automotive software engineering centres
milestone: A second entrant announced a Sfax centre, May 2026
position_start: An American supplier's Tunisian hub, its only one for the Middle East and Africa, past 100 million dollars of cumulative investment with nearly 200 software engineers against a target of 500, and a 20,000 square metre factory extension of about 85 million dollars
