position_end: An Indian mobility-technology firm committed 1.52 million dollars to a new software-engineering centre at Sfax serving global carmakers, taking the export-oriented engineering base beyond the existing coastal hubs
note: both figures come from the investment promotion agency's own announcements; no employment or export series for the sector is held

subject: tech.industry
name: Information and communication sector value added
milestone: 4,894.4 million dinars in 2025, against 3,469.1 million in 2020
position_start: 3,469.1 million dinars of gross value added at current prices in 2020
position_end: 4,894.4 million dinars in 2025 on the same national-accounts series
note: current prices, so the series carries inflation as well as growth and no volume measure is published alongside it

subject: tech.industry
name: Telecommunications market structure
milestone: Regulator data showing mobile broadband as the dominant access point
position_start: Three mobile operators, mobile internet and subscriptions rising and voice plateauing under displacement by internet services (2025-04)
position_end: Unchanged in structure; the state operator is being modernised under a European development loan and the market's two private operators are foreign groups (2026-08)

subject: tech.innovate
name: BridgeTech business matchmaking platform
milestone: Handed to the American chamber of commerce, 8 June 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a locally held asset
position_end: The United States ambassador handed the matchmaking platform to the American chamber of commerce in June 2026, converting a 3.3 million dollar business-support project running since 2019 into a continuing startup and business matchmaking mechanism
note: no user, deal or match count is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup Act and Startup Tunisia
milestone: Diaspora programme opened 2026-08-27
position_start: In force, with over 40 firms reported as having expanded into Europe, the Middle East and sub-Saharan Africa (2025-08)
position_end: In force and being circulated as a replicable model rather than as one country's statute, through a triangular programme with Japan (2026-07)

subject: tech.innovate
name: Tunisia Digital Summit
milestone: Tenth edition held, April 2026
position_end: Tenth edition held with about 2,000 participants and 80 exhibitors, the minister setting a goal of a regional digital hub and pledging continued legal and regulatory development on artificial intelligence and data protection (2026-04)

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Continuing digital training for civil servants at the ENA
milestone: January to October 2026 online batch opened
position_start: A statutory continuing-training framework, in force since 1993 and amended in 1995, under which the school's digital-skills courses run
position_end: A January to October 2026 batch of online courses for agents nominated by their ministries, including one on e-administration and open government, with a certificate conditional on completing the course and passing tests
note: no source separately measures digital literacy across the civil service, only the training offered to it

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital skills in the development plan
milestone: Named in the plan annex approved by law in July 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a statutory commitment
position_end: Artificial intelligence, data analysis, programming and cybersecurity named as the skills base of a digital economy made a pillar of human-capital development; no programme, budget, target or delivery agency is stated (2026-06)

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital training for women entrepreneurs
milestone: First cohort of 100 opened, August 2026
position_end: The family and women's ministry, a national entrepreneurs' organisation and a UN regional commission opened a training programme for 100 women entrepreneurs in e-commerce and artificial-intelligence applications, alongside a national platform for marketing women's products; both sit under a declaration on women, youth, digitalisation and African economic integration whose action plan to 2030 targets training 100,000 women and young people in e-commerce, AI and cross-border digital payments by 2028, and a US$50m fund for inclusive markets by 2028
note: the training launch's own date is not established in the source

subject: capacity.training
name: El-Khawarizmi computing centre high-performance system
milestone: Inaugurated 23 July 2026
position_end: Tunisia's first high-performance computing system, a Chinese donation installed by SOHO, ZTE and DSHELL at the Centre de Calcul El-Khawarizmi, intended for artificial intelligence, big data and simulation across the higher-education and research system
note: nothing states how access is allocated between institutions

subject: capacity.training
name: Informatique in the secondary curriculum
milestone: Listed in the ministry's curriculum index, on a 2008 curriculum text
position_start: A formal secondary-education subject alongside mathematics and physical sciences
position_end: Unchanged on the record; no enrolment, pass-rate or teacher-coverage figure is held

subject: capacity.training
name: National certifying training programme for teaching staff
milestone: Registration opened 4 to 12 April 2026
position_end: 2,500 primary and secondary teachers targeted for distance training on Certiport, ITS, PMI and Microsoft content, with 1,000 places sitting certification exams
note: no completion or certification outcome is held

subject: capacity.research
name: ITES study on artificial intelligence and the social state
milestone: Published 11 December 2025
position_end: The first Tunisian study on artificial intelligence as a lever for the social role of the state, carrying 143 recommendations across five sectors and built with about 125 participants
note: nothing on the record states what the state did with the recommendations

subject: include.access
name: Accessibility of public services and the disability card platform
milestone: Disability card platform launched December 2025
position_start: A 2019 government circular instructs all public bodies to facilitate physical access, priority service, Braille, sign-language and audio aids, accessible bilingual or trilingual websites with resizable and auto-read text, and staff training, naming persons with disabilities as the first of seven priority categories
position_end: The social affairs ministry launched a digital platform for the disability card in December 2025 — electronic document upload, tracking through the citizen space, remote renewal and a QR-coded smart card — removing a physical-presence barrier
note: the standing instrument is a circular rather than a statute, and no audit of public-site accessibility against it is held

subject: include.access
name: Affordability of digital services
milestone: Regulator's affordability report on international data, July 2026
position_end: A digital basket at 1.53% of gross national income per head, about US$5.31 a month, second in the Maghreb and under the two-percent international threshold; the figures are the international union's, reported by the regulator (2026-07)
note: Cited as a reference measurement, not absorbed as country state.

subject: include.access
name: e-Mowaten citizen feedback and petition portal
milestone: Monthly remote training for public agents opened September 2025
position_start: Constituted by decree in December 2019 as a national participation and interaction system letting users file petitions, proposals, notifications and guidance requests and track them online to an electronically signed reply, with processing assigned to citizen-relations offices and central management at the head of government's citizen relations office
position_end: The national school of administration opened a rolling monthly remote training programme for public agents on the portal from September 2025, implementing a decision of the major projects committee so that citizens can report difficulties with administrative services immediately
note: no petition volume, response time or resolution rate is published; the training notice's own date is uncertain between 1 and 15 September 2025

subject: include.access
name: National digital marketplace for women's products
milestone: Launched 12 August 2026
position_end: The family and women's ministry launched a national digital marketplace for women's and girls' products, with payment and delivery agreements with the postal service and a partnership with the handicrafts office, giving home-based craftswomen direct access to national markets
note: no seller count, transaction volume or gender-disaggregated digital-access measure is held

subject: data.statistics
name: Business statistics from the Repertoire National des Entreprises
milestone: 2023 edition published 3 June 2025
position_start: An annual statistical output derived from the business register, itself fed by tax and social-security administrative files
position_end: Unchanged in form; the 2023 edition is the most recent in the series

subject: data.statistics
name: Code de l'information statistique and SNDS 2026-2030
milestone: Still in drafting in June 2026, after a promised end-2025 finalisation
movement: Stalled, the end-2025 finalisation date passed with the text still in drafting
position_start: Announced for finalisation by the end of 2025, with wide consultations in 2026
position_end: Being drafted alongside the national statistics development strategy 2026-2030 and intended to replace the 1999 law, covering big data, administrative-data access, the governance roles of the statistical council and institute, and staff retention; no text and no adoption date is published
note: the SNDS 2026-2030 is named on the record but not published on it

subject: data.statistics
name: Internet use
milestone: Regulator's own results summary published, July 2026
position_end: 85.9% of respondents using the internet, 95.4% holding a mobile line, 84.3% a smartphone and 41% a computer, with 70.4% of internet users connecting principally over mobile. Among internet users, 41.3% use an e-service, 36.9% e-commerce, 26.5% e-government and 47.9% artificial intelligence (2026)
note: the survey is the observatory's first to measure digital-skills use as well as access; no earlier edition on this series is held, so the figures are levels and not directions

subject: data.statistics
name: Linkage of the 2024 census with social-scheme administrative records
milestone: Bulletin published September 2025
position_end: Census results combined with CNSS, CNRPS, CNAM and Amen Social records to produce social-coverage indicators — 66.3 per cent effective social-security coverage of the occupied population, 82.1 per cent health coverage and SDG indicator 1.3.1 at 65.7 per cent — broken down by sex, age, governorate and employment status
note: no data-sharing instrument between the statistics institute and the social schemes is held

subject: data.statistics
name: Population projections 2025-2054
milestone: New Bayesian series on the 2024 census, published May 2026
position_end: A projection series to 2054 built on the 2024 census population of 11.97 million and on civil-registration data, using a UN-standard Bayesian methodology
note: the full brochure's text layer does not extract cleanly; the landing page is what is held

subject: data.statistics
name: Use of online public administration
milestone: National observatory survey reported July 2026
position_end: 26.5% of internet users, last of the four uses measured, behind artificial-intelligence applications at 47.9%, e-services at 41.3% and online shopping at 36.9% (2026)

subject: data.open
name: Agrifood sector data portal
milestone: Launched 23 July 2026 after a full functional test on 9 July
position_end: Live and free after registration, centralising regulatory monitoring, market movement, export opportunity and sector-trend data under three public bodies; built inside a German- and EU-financed project with no amount disclosed and no statement of what happens when the project ends (2026-07)

subject: data.open
name: Aswat Nissa femicide data platform
milestone: Launch announced for 12 August 2026, the eve of National Women's Day
position_end: A civil-society platform to centralise Tunisia's femicide data, opening the 109 cases documented since January 2018 (30 in 2025, 26 in 2024, 25 in 2023, 23 in 2022) to researchers, media and civil-society organisations; launch set for 12 August 2026, with no state role or public-data reconciliation stated (2026-08)
note: An NGO-run platform, not a state system; included for Tunisia's gender-based-violence data infrastructure, a gap flagged by UNODC's 2025 global meeting on femicide measurement.

subject: data.open
name: Decree 2021-3 on open public data
milestone: Gazetted 6 January 2021
position_start: Establishes opening by default, the national open-data portal, the e-government unit's governance duties, a joint consultative committee, an open-data officer in every public body, and metadata, quality, licensing and dataset-inventory rules
position_end: Unchanged and still the operative backbone; no later standalone data-governance or open-data instrument supersedes it
note: no dataset inventory, publication count or list of designated open-data officers is held

subject: data.open
name: National public data registry (registre.data.gov.tn)
milestone: Confirmed live and enabling citizen data requests, per the Open Government Partnership's Independent Reporting Mechanism report published 4 August 2026
position_end: Launched by the E-Government Unit, letting citizens view and request inventoried government data; named among the only commitments of Tunisia's 2023-2025 open-government action plan to produce results citizens can see, against a National Open Data Strategy that still awaits formal government endorsement (2026-08)
note: Findings of the Open Government Partnership's Independent Reporting Mechanism review, an evaluation report cited for this specific finding rather than absorbed in full; the registry's own launch date is not given.

subject: data.open
name: National strategy for the governance, opening and valorisation of public data
milestone: Final draft workshopped 26 March 2026
position_end: The final draft of the country's first dedicated strategy for the governance, opening and valorisation of public data was presented and discussed at a March 2026 workshop, implementing the 2021 decree; it is a draft under consultation and not an adopted instrument
note: an evaluation report separately records the strategy as still awaiting formal government endorsement

subject: data.satellite
name: FAO WaPOR water-productivity monitoring
milestone: Jendouba pilot lifted the data to 10 metres daily, March 2026
position_start: Remote-sensing work on water productivity with the agriculture ministry, the Institut de l'Olivier, the Institut National des Grandes Cultures and the meteorology institute, including crop-mapping fieldwork in Jendouba and Kairouan
position_end: A Jendouba pilot raised evapotranspiration data from 20 metres dekadal to 10 metres daily for the IREY irrigation-advisory app, flagging irrigation need about a week earlier and cutting overestimation by roughly 10 per cent
note: donor-led; no national agricultural remote-sensing programme run by the state itself is held

subject: data.satellite
name: Meteosat reception and exploitation at the meteorology institute
milestone: Third-generation satellite data in use alongside a new national radar network
position_start: Meteosat data used since the 1980s for flood and drought early warning, on progressively upgraded receiving and exploitation systems
position_end: Third-generation satellite data in use alongside a new national radar network, 150 automatic surface stations and 125 new rain-gauge stations, with the institute claiming 99 to 100 per cent accuracy for real-time forecasts
note: the accuracy figure is the institute's own and nothing on the record tests it

subject: data.satellite
name: SWAMED satellite and drone irrigation monitoring
milestone: Started 1 August 2025
position_end: An EU Interreg NEXT MED project with a budget of EUR 2,745,200 deploying real-time satellite and drone irrigation-water monitoring and an artificial-intelligence decision-support system at a Tunisian pilot site among four Mediterranean sites

subject: geopol.usa
name: United States digital cooperation with Tunisia
status: Implemented, no state-level instrument on record
milestone: Embassy programme handed to the American chamber of commerce, June 2026
position_end: The clearest American record is a 2021 embassy-funded fintech programme pairing Tunisian startups with Amazon Web Services, IBM and Microsoft, each participating startup receiving 11,500 dollars of free cloud services; a 3.3 million dollar business-matchmaking project closed in June 2026 with its platform handed to the American chamber of commerce; and in December 2025 the second mobile operator announced a Google Cloud deployment of Vertex AI and Gemini models through a managed-services partner. No hyperscaler-specific memorandum, capital investment or state-level instrument is held
note: the 2021 programme's continuation past its project term is unconfirmed

subject: geopol.china
name: Chinese digital cooperation with Tunisia
milestone: A donated high-performance computing system inaugurated 23 July 2026
position_start: An inter-ministerial memorandum on information and communication technology cooperation signed at Tianjin on 27 June 2023, scoped to digital infrastructure, digital-technology applications, and network and data security
position_end: An education cloud summit opened in Tunis in December 2025 by the Chinese ambassador and the higher-education minister, with about 300 participants from the defence, health, communication technologies and education ministries and commitments on both sides to deepen higher-education digitalisation and artificial-intelligence cooperation; a Chinese donation then delivered the country's first high-performance computing system in July 2026
note: no later Chinese-government record of the memorandum's renewal, amendment or expiry was located

subject: geopol.eu
name: EU-Tunisia strategic and global partnership memorandum
milestone: Signed at Tunis, 16 July 2023
position_end: A non-binding political framework whose digital-transition section commits both parties to cooperate on capacity building, technological cooperation, financing and joint projects, names the Medusa submarine cable as a connectivity opportunity and Tunisia's potential role as an Africa connectivity hub, and undertakes to assess Tunisian participation in the Digital Europe Programme
note: nothing held records whether the Digital Europe Programme assessment was carried out

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf operator engagement in the Tunisian telecommunications sector
milestone: Qatari group reports 12 per cent Tunisian revenue growth for 2025
position_start: The national operator named in May 2023 as the first to join an Emirati group's partner-network programme, reaffirmed in that group's February 2024 results
position_end: A Qatari group's 2025 results record its Tunisian unit's revenue up 12 per cent to QAR 1,726 million, accelerating fixed-broadband and 5G fixed-wireless investment after a full commercial launch in February 2025, and confirm its Tunisian fintech subsidiary, licensed early in 2025, on track for an app release in the first quarter of 2026
note: both are corporate results releases; no Gulf-state digital-sector memorandum with Tunisia is held

subject: geopol.india
name: Indian digital cooperation with Tunisia
milestone: Joint working team and two draft memoranda agreed, May 2026
position_end: The communication technologies minister and the Indian ambassador discussed capacity building, expertise exchange, Tunisian participation in India's global artificial-intelligence summit and joint digital-transformation projects in January 2026; in May the two health ministries agreed a joint working team and two draft memoranda, on medical tourism and drug manufacturing, with expert exchange on digital health and telemedicine. Nothing is signed
note: two draft memoranda and a working team; no signed instrument, line of credit or programme document naming Tunisia is held
